What factor of a wetland affects migratory birds? and if the factor changes in the future, how will behaviour change?

```{r load package, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ranger)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(zoo)
```

```{r}
crane_data <- read.csv("/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/Grus_Vipio/GPScrane_covariates.csv")

train_df <- crane_data %>%
  # Convert 'time' to a proper datetime object just in case we need it for seasonality later. Date_Time
  mutate(time = ymd_hms(time)) %>%
  arrange(Station, time) %>% 
  group_by(Station) %>%
  select(
    time, Station,
    Temperature.C., Wind_Speed.m.s., SPI6_Smooth,
    Water_Temp_Smooth, BOD_Smooth, DTN_Smooth, Chlorophyll_Smooth
  ) %>%
  drop_na() #%>%

meteo_vars <- c("Temperature.C.", "Wind_Speed.m.s.", "SPI6_Smooth", "Station")
```

=========================================
Random Forest pipeline for 2031–2050 data
=========================================
Meteo -> Water_Temp -> BOD & DTN -> Chlorophyll

Step 1: The Physical Base
Input: Meteorological variables (Air Temp, Wind Speed, SPI6).
Target: Predict Water Temperature.

Step 2: The Chemical State
Input: Meteorological variables + Predicted Water Temperature.
Target: Predict DTN and BOD (as nutrient cycling and oxygen demand are highly dependent on water temperature).

Step 3: The Biological Response with Lag (The "Chain Memory" Method)
Input: Meteorological variables + Predicted Water Temp + Predicted DTN + Predicted BOD.
Target: Predict Chlorophyll.

```{r}
set.seed(100)
print("Training Model 1: Water Temperature...")
# Water_Temp_Smooth ~ Temperature.C. + Wind_Speed.m.s. + SPI6_Smooth + Station
form_wtemp <- as.formula(paste("Water_Temp_Smooth ~", paste(meteo_vars, collapse = " + ")))
rf_wtemp <- ranger(formula = form_wtemp, data = train_df, importance = 'permutation')
train_df$Pred_Water_Temp <- rf_wtemp$predictions

print("Training Model 2 & 3: BOD and DTN...")
# BOD/DTN_Smooth ~ Temperature.C. + Wind_Speed.m.s. + SPI6_Smooth + Station + Pred_Water_Temp
form_chem <- as.formula(paste(" ~", paste(c(meteo_vars, "Pred_Water_Temp"), collapse = " + ")))
rf_bod <- ranger(formula = update(BOD_Smooth ~ ., form_chem), data = train_df)
rf_dtn <- ranger(formula = update(DTN_Smooth ~ ., form_chem), data = train_df)
train_df$Pred_BOD <- rf_bod$predictions
train_df$Pred_DTN <- rf_dtn$predictions
```

```{r}
print("Training Model 4: Chlorophyll-a...")
# Chlorophyll_Smooth ~ Temperature.C. + Wind_Speed.m.s. + SPI6_Smooth + Station + Mem_Pred_WTemp + Mem_Pred_BOD + Mem_Pred_DTN

train_df <- train_df %>%
  arrange(Station, time) %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  mutate(
    # 3-day rolling averages of the chemical outputs, k=72 steps (36 hours), "right"=look at past.
    Mem_Pred_WTemp = rollmean(Pred_Water_Temp, k = 72, fill = NA, align = "right"), 
    Mem_Pred_BOD = rollmean(Pred_BOD, k = 72, fill = NA, align = "right"),
    Mem_Pred_DTN = rollmean(Pred_DTN, k = 72, fill = NA, align = "right")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  drop_na(Mem_Pred_WTemp) # Drop the first 72 hours of the dataset where the rolling average couldn't compute

set.seed(100)
form_bio <- as.formula(paste("Chlorophyll_Smooth ~", 
                             paste(c(meteo_vars, "Mem_Pred_WTemp", "Mem_Pred_BOD", "Mem_Pred_DTN"), 
                                   collapse = " + ")))
rf_chl <- ranger(formula = form_bio, data = train_df, importance = 'permutation')
train_df$Pred_Chlorophyll <- rf_chl$predictions
```

```{r, fig.width=5.2, fig.height=4.5}
library(patchwork)
# ---------------------------------------------------------

imp_data <- tibble(

        plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust=0.5), axis.title = element_text(size = 9) )

final_plot <- (plot_imp | plot_scatter) / plot_time
print(final_plot)
```

```{r}
library(ncdf4)

nc_path <- "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/wetland_birds/data/Wetland_2006_2023/Korea_2000_2019_yearly_climate/평균기온_MKPRISMv21_skorea_TA_gridraw_yearly_2000_2019.nc"
nc_raw <- nc_open(nc_path)

lon_array <- as.numeric(ncvar_get(nc_raw, "longitude"))
lat_array <- as.numeric(ncvar_get(nc_raw, "latitude"))
nc_close(nc_raw) #1D axes (601X751)
grid_coords <- expand.grid(lon = lon_array, lat = lat_array)
print(paste("Total grid cells reconstructed:", nrow(grid_coords)))

targets <- data.frame(
  Station = c("Paju", "Cheorwon"),
  lon = c(126.79618, 127.3113),
  lat = c(37.76469, 38.1485) )

find_closest_grid <- function(t_lon, t_lat, grid_df) {
  # Calculate Euclidean distance (straight line)
  dists <- sqrt((grid_df$lon - t_lon)^2 + (grid_df$lat - t_lat)^2)
  # Return the exact ROW number (which corresponds to the .txt COLUMN index)
  return(which.min(dists))
}
paju_idx <- find_closest_grid(targets$lon[1], targets$lat[1], grid_coords)
cheorwon_idx <- find_closest_grid(targets$lon[2], targets$lat[2], grid_coords)

print(paste("Paju Index:", paju_idx))
print(paste("Cheorwon Index:", cheorwon_idx))
print(paste("Paju Grid Center is at: Lon", grid_coords$lon[paju_idx], "Lat", grid_coords$lat[paju_idx]))
print(paste("Cheorwon Grid Center is at: Lon", grid_coords$lon[cheorwon_idx], "Lat", grid_coords$lat[cheorwon_idx]))
```

```{r}
library(data.table)
extracted_list <- list()
ssp_folder <- "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/Grus_Vipio/SSP/realistic/windspeed_SSP245_2031_2050_asc"
  #windspeed_SSP245_2031_2050_asc #temperature_SSP245_2031_2050_asc

# Loop through the years you want to extract (e.g., 2031 to 2050)
for (yr in 2031:2050) {
  file_path <- file.path(ssp_folder, paste0("AR6_SSP245_5ENSMN_skorea_WS_gridraw_daily_", yr, ".txt")) 
  #"AR6_SSP245_5ENSMN_skorea_WS_gridraw_daily_"  #"AR6_SSP245_5ENSMN_skorea_TA_gridraw_daily_"
  if(file.exists(file_path)) {
    print(paste("Extracting year:", yr))
    # fread opens the 1GB file, grabs ONLY the two numeric columns, and closes it.
    # header = FALSE ensures the first row of data isn't accidentally deleted/used as names.
    temp_data <- fread(file_path, select = c(paju_idx, cheorwon_idx), header = FALSE)
    names(temp_data) <- c("Paju", "Cheorwon")
    dates <- seq(from = ymd(paste0(yr, "-01-01")), 
                 to = ymd(paste0(yr, "-12-31")), 
                 by = "day")
    # If it's a leap year (366 dates) but the climate model only outputs 365 days...
    if (length(dates) == 366 && nrow(temp_data) == 365) {
      # Remove February 29th from our generated R timeline!
      dates <- dates[!(month(dates) == 2 & day(dates) == 29)]
    }
    temp_data$Date <- dates
    extracted_list[[as.character(yr)]] <- temp_data
  } else {
    print(paste("Warning: File not found for year", yr))
  }
}
all_years_df <- bind_rows(extracted_list)
print(head(all_years_df))
```

#SPI6 file had different format.
```{r}
ssp_folder <- "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/Grus_Vipio/SSP"
spi6_file_path <- file.path(ssp_folder, "SPI6_SSP245_monthly_2021_2100.txt")

if(file.exists(spi6_file_path)) {
  spi6_data <- fread(spi6_file_path, select = c(paju_idx, cheorwon_idx), header = FALSE)
  names(spi6_data) <- c("Paju", "Cheorwon")
  # Generate timeline anchored to the 1st of the month
  monthly_dates <- seq(from = ymd("2021-01-01"), 
                       to = ymd("2100-12-01"), 
                       by = "month") # 80 years * 12 months = 960 rows expected.
  # Safety check: Ensure the file length matches our calendar
  if(nrow(spi6_data) == length(monthly_dates)) {
    spi6_data$Date <- monthly_dates
  } else {
    print(paste("Warning: Mismatch! File has", nrow(spi6_data), "rows, but calendar has", length(monthly_dates)))
    # Fallback just in case the file is short
    spi6_data$Date <- monthly_dates[1:nrow(spi6_data)] 
  }
  # Slice out exactly the 2031-2050 window you need for your model
  extracted_spi6 <- spi6_data %>%
    filter(year(Date) >= 2031 & year(Date) <= 2050)
} else {
  print("Error: Could not find the SPI6 file. Please check the file name!")
}

all_years_df <- bind_rows(extracted_spi6)
print(head(all_years_df))
```

```{r}
# INTERPOLATE every 30 minute
library(zoo)
#merged_ssp <- temp_ssp %>%
#  left_join(wind_ssp, by = c("Station", "Date_Time")) %>%
#  left_join(spi6_ssp, by = c("Station", "Date_Time"))
#write_csv(merged_ssp, "/Users/yjkang/Desktop/SSP_2031_2050_temp_wind_SPI6.csv")
merged_ssp <-read_csv("/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/Grus_Vipio/SSP/realistic/SSP245_2031_2050_temp_wind_SPI6.csv")
  
# Create a master hourly grid for 2031-2050
hourly_grid <- expand_grid(
  Station = c("Paju", "Cheorwon"),
  Date_Time = seq(
    from = ymd_hms("2031-01-01 00:00:00"), 
    to = ymd_hms("2050-12-31 23:00:00"), 
    by = "30 min" #hour
  )
)
future_ssp_df <- hourly_grid %>%
  # Join our daily/monthly data onto the hourly timeline (this creates lots of NAs)
  left_join(merged_ssp, by = c("Station", "Date_Time")) %>%
  arrange(Station, Date_Time) %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  # Fill the NAs by drawing a smooth mathematical curve through the daily noon points!
  mutate(
    Temperature.C. = na.spline(Temp_Daily, na.rm = FALSE),
    Wind_Speed.m.s. = na.spline(Wind_Daily, na.rm = FALSE),
    SPI6_Smooth = na.spline(SPI6_Monthly, na.rm = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
head(future_ssp_df)
```

```{r}
set.seed(100)
# ==========================================
# RUNNING THE REGRESSOR CHAIN
# ==========================================
print("Projecting future Water Temperature...")
future_df$Pred_Water_Temp <- predict(rf_wtemp, data = future_df)$predictions

print("Projecting future BOD and DTN...")
future_df$Pred_BOD <- predict(rf_bod, data = future_df)$predictions
future_df$Pred_DTN <- predict(rf_dtn, data = future_df)$predictions

# ==========================================
# APPLYING BIOLOGICAL LAG TO FUTURE
# ==========================================
print("Applying 36-hour biological lag to future chemical predictions...")
future_df <- future_df %>%
  arrange(Station, Date_Time) %>%
  group_by(Station) %>%
  mutate(
    Mem_Pred_WTemp = rollmean(Pred_Water_Temp, k = 72, fill = NA, align = "right"),
    Mem_Pred_BOD = rollmean(Pred_BOD, k = 72, fill = NA, align = "right"),
    Mem_Pred_DTN = rollmean(Pred_DTN, k = 72, fill = NA, align = "right")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  drop_na(Mem_Pred_WTemp)

# ==========================================
# FINAL BIOLOGICAL PROJECTION
# ==========================================
print("Projecting future Chlorophyll-a...")
future_df$Pred_Chlorophyll <- predict(rf_chl, data = future_df)$predictions

#select the winter seasons only, since the model was strictly limited to winters.
future_df <- future_df %>%
  filter(month(Date_Time) %in% c(10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4))
```

```{r}
future_env <- read.csv("/Users/yjkang/Desktop/NIE_BigData/Grus_Vipio/SSP/realistic/future_env_2031_2050_1hr.csv")

  mutate(

    Fut_Temp   = Temperature.C.,

    Fut_SPI6   = SPI6_Smooth,
```

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
hist_df <- comb_env %>%
  select(Station, Month_Date, Temp, Wind, wTemp, BOD, Chlor, DTN, SPI6) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Temp, Wind, wTemp, BOD, Chlor, DTN, SPI6), names_to = "Variable",values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(Period = "Historical",nVariable = str_replace(Variable, "Han_", ""))
fut_df <- comb_env %>%
  select(Station, Month_Date, starts_with("Fut_")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("Fut_"),names_to = "Variable",values_to = "Value") %>%
  mutate(Period = "Future",Variable = str_replace(Variable, "Fut_", ""))
combined_df <- bind_rows(hist_df, fut_df) %>% filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = c("Temp", "Wind", "SPI6", "wTemp", "BOD", "DTN", "Chlor")), 
         Period = factor(Period, levels = c("Historical", "Future")) )
mu_df <- combined_df %>%
  group_by(Variable, Period) %>%
  summarise(grp_mean = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

distribution_plot <- ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = Value, fill = Period)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(data = mu_df, aes(xintercept = grp_mean, color = Period, linetype=Period), linewidth = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Variable, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Historical" = "grey", "Future" = "dodgerblue3"),
                    labels = c("Historical" = "Historical (2016-2024)", "Future" = "Future (2031-2050)"), name = NULL) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Historical" = "grey20", "Future" = "dodgerblue4"), labels =NULL, name = NULL) +
  labs(y = "Probability Density",fill = "") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.48, 0.08), panel.spacing.y = unit(20, "pt"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10) )
print(distribution_plot)
ggsave("/Users/yjkang/Desktop/env_shift.pdf", plot=distribution_plot, height=4, width=8)
```

```{r}
library(effectsize)

effect_size_results <- combined_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(Period) == 2) %>%
  do(as.data.frame(rank_biserial(Value ~ Period, data = .)))

print(effect_size_results)
```
Effect sizes evaluated based on their absolute values ($|r_{rb}|$) using the following standard thresholds:
$|r_{rb}| < 0.10$: Negligible effect
$0.10 \le |r_{rb}| < 0.30$: Small effect
$0.30 \le |r_{rb}| < 0.50$: Moderate effect
$|r_{rb}| \ge 0.50$: Large effect
